title: Commits that read like a story, because somebody will read them

videos.script: In a job, your commits are read by the people you work with, every day. In a portfolio, they are read by one person, once, deciding whether they want to work with you. {{once}} A history of twenty commits called fix, wip and stuff tells them nothing, except that you did not expect anybody to look. A history where each line says what changed, in the order it changed, tells them how you work, without a word of explanation. {{story}} loanbook's history reads that way. Three habits produced it: a reason in every message, one change per commit, and tidying before you push.
